_: Which core test projects a change runs (docs/design/architecture-review.md step 6.3, docs/TESTING_LAYERS.md). modules.mjs reads it; gates.sh and land.sh ask it.

A changed path belongs to the FIRST module whose paths match it (globs: * within a folder, ** across folders), or for the Chemistry test files to the module whose 'props' names its item list in core/Chem.Tests.props: that split is read from the props file, never copied here.

'projects' are code: those core projects run, and every project that references them (ProjectReferences, followed transitively; Chem.Tests.props's count for each project that imports it). A library (Game.Core, Rules.Mcp) runs its dependents.
'reads' are data: those test projects read the files, and run alone (who references them doesn't matter).
A module with neither runs no dotnet tests (docs, tools). A path in no module runs everything: the fail-safe.

Every Chem.* project but Chem.Land.Tests links the Runtime through Game.Core, so each Runtime area in Game.Core runs everything but the land's own tests; 'after' says which project it narrows to once it's an assembly of its own. Chemistry/Mcp and Playtest/Logic compile into Game.Core too, so they run the same. The land (Chem.Land, below Game.Core) and the modes (Chem.Play, above it) are assemblies of their own.
'stop' (step 5c): projects whose dependents aren't followed for that module's changes; what's past them gets the smoke. runtime-land stops at Game.Core (Andrew, 2026-11-26). check takes the same cut.
core/ files in no module (Chem.Tests.props, Directory.Build.props, the solution, the runsettings, TestParallel.cs, TestFriends.cs) run everything, as any unmapped path does.
modules.mjs check (run by gates.test.mjs) proves the map agrees with the csproj files: every file a project compiles must select that project.

modules.name: runtime-land
modules._: Chem.Land's own assembly (step 5a). Andrew's ruling (2026-11-26, step 5c): a Land change runs Chem.Land.Tests and Chem.LandWorld.Tests (they reference Chem.Land), and not what reaches it only through Game.Core: those get the Unit smoke, and CI's full run after every push to dev catches the rest. Its adapters onto a world (World.Land, GeneratedSource, BakedSource, MapBake, MapCheck, GeneratedPlaces, CellHeightfield, OpenWorld*) are Sim's: runtime-sim, everything.

modules.name: runtime-golf
modules._: Spell golf, a mini-game on its own assembly (D22, docs/design/minigames.md): a golf change runs Chem.Play.Golf.Tests, and Playtest.Text and Rules.Mcp build on it. It stops at Rules.Mcp (the MCP server's rooms install golf): Rules.Mcp.Tests and Chat.Bench reach golf only through it, so they get the Unit smoke, and CI's full run after every push to dev catches the rest (as runtime-land's stop at Game.Core, 2026-11-26).

modules.name: runtime-play
modules._: Chem.Play's own assembly (architecture-review.md step 9): the Hold's, the defense field's and the course's systems, above Game.Core. A Play change runs what references Chem.Play: Chem.Play.Tests, Hold.Runner (and its tests) and Playtest.Text, and the rest get the Unit smoke. No stop is needed: nothing heavy reaches Chem.Play, and nothing below it (Game.Core and what's on it) can, so the cut is the references themselves. The modes' state, its save and the seam (World.Play.cs, IWorldModes.cs, Hold.cs, Defense.cs, Course.cs, HoldRun.cs) and the raiders and the dragon are Sim's, as are the modes' contract and bodies (WorldMode.cs, Body.cs, World.Bodies.cs): runtime-sim, everything.

modules.name: tests-lockstep-kit
modules._: The late-join harness (LockstepKit.cs, D22): a library; the lockstep tests and the modes' tests that reference it run.

modules.name: plans-tests
modules._: The view plans' tests (step 6): Unity's Prototype.Plans.Tests, and core/Prototype.Plans.Tests on Prototype.Plans alone.

modules.name: plans
modules._: The view plans (step 6): Unity's Prototype.Plans, core/Prototype.Plans with the UnityMath shim. HiddenThingTests reads them as it reads the rest of the view.

modules.name: view-code
modules._: No dotnet project compiles the view; Rules.Mcp.Tests's HiddenThingTests reads every non-test .cs under unity/Assets/Prototype.

modules.name: view-assets
modules._: Scenes, prefabs, .meta, art: no dotnet project or test reads them.

modules.name: core-plans
modules._: The plans' project and the shim it links in place of UnityEngine.

modules.name: core-chat-fixtures
modules._: Chat.Bench.Tests compiles ChatFixtures.cs and reads chat-fixtures/.

modules.name: rules
modules._: Every test that loads ChemistryTests.R, Rules.Mcp's tools, the Hold curve; not Playtest.Runner.Tests or Prototype.Plans.Tests (no rules).

modules.name: world
modules._: The maps, biomes, golf, landmarks: the same readers as rules/ (the valley is every test world's default), and the plans' FarMeshesTests (world/horizon.json).

modules.name: docs-read-by-tests
modules._: GameFoldersTests checks GLOSSARY.md is there; LiveRulesTests reads MODDING.md.

modules.name: sandbox
modules._: Frozen; its own gates run when it changed (SANDBOX_GATES).
